comparator.name: Tax Law
comparator.sourceNotes: The live Leiden Study Guide identifies a three-year, 180-EC Tax Law bachelor. The first year establishes a broad Dutch-law foundation and introduces tax law and legal methods. The second year combines private, criminal, European and company law with individual income taxation, value added and real-estate transfer taxation, financial accounting, public-sector economics and the ethics of taxation. The third year requires tax-law moot court, procedural and formal tax law, public-sector economics, tax ethics, international tax law, corporation tax and a bachelor thesis, while preserving 15 EC of genuine elective space. No formal route or specialisation is required for the generic normalized target; the programme's full-time curriculum supplies the academically neutral content reconstruction for the registered full-time and part-time modes.

exception.reason: Leiden Tax Law is a cumulative Dutch legal degree with a specialist fiscal spine. Its compulsory curriculum combines the foundations of constitutional, private, criminal, international, European, administrative, Roman, obligations and company law with income taxation, value added and real-estate transfer taxation, corporation tax, international tax law, procedural and formal tax law, financial accounting, public-sector economics, tax ethics, fiscal advocacy and a Tax Law thesis. UCR offers a useful six-course law-and-justice sequence plus economics, public economics, accounting and business-law courses, but no dedicated tax-law course or progression in income, corporate, indirect, international, procedural and formal taxation. A 24-course UCR pathway could examine law, markets and public policy broadly, but it could not preserve the target's academic identity as Tax Law.
exception.curriculumContext: The current 2026-2027 curriculum accounts for the full 180 EC: 60 EC of first-year legal foundations, 60 EC of second-year legal and fiscal study, and a third year comprising 40 EC of compulsory advanced fiscal study, 15 EC of genuine elective space and a 5-EC Tax Law thesis. Across years 2 and 3 the required specialist courses form a connected progression through individual income taxation, indirect taxation, financial accounting, public-sector economics and tax ethics into procedural and formal tax law, international taxation, corporation tax and fiscal moot-court practice. The programme therefore cannot be represented by a few isolated courses about taxation or public policy.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. GOSGATE102 Law, Society & Justice, GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, GOSLAWJ211 Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law, GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law, GOSLAWJ311 Principles of Private Law and GOSLAWJ312 Foundations of European Union Law provide meaningful broad legal formation. BENECON111 Introduction to Economics, BENECON211 International Macroeconomics, BENECON212 Microeconomics & Behavior, BENECON311 Public Economics and BENECON312 Econometrics provide economic and policy analysis; BENBUSI112 Accounting & Corporate Finance and BENBUSI311 Transnational Business Law add adjacent accounting and business-law study. Public Economics explicitly addresses taxation, public goods, externalities and government spending, but the workbook contains no dedicated tax law, individual income taxation, corporation tax, value added or transfer tax, international taxation, fiscal procedure, formal tax law, taxpayer-rights or tax-enforcement course, no Dutch administrative and obligations-law progression, and no fiscal moot court or Tax Law thesis. The closest possible UCR combination would consequently be an interdisciplinary law-and-economics pathway, not a defensible substitute for the comparator's specialist fiscal-law sequence.
